ev.k6_storyteller.title: The Storyteller
ev.k6_storyteller.text: A wandering storyteller came to the square - grey-haired, with a staff and a voice that hushed even the dogs. He told of a hero who went down into the land of the dead, and at the most terrifying moment he stopped: the rest tomorrow, for a treat.
ev.k6_storyteller.give: Give him your supper, just to hear the ending
ev.k6_storyteller.give.ok: You sat hungry all evening and never regretted it once. The hero came back from the land of the dead, and you carried every word home.
ev.k6_storyteller.sneak: Sneak into the front row tomorrow without a treat
ev.k6_storyteller.sneak.success: The storyteller winked at you and pretended not to notice. The ending was better than you had dreamed.
ev.k6_storyteller.sneak.failure: The storyteller stopped mid-sentence and asked, in front of everyone, where your treat was. Every head turned. You ran off and never heard the ending.
ev.k6_storyteller.invent.ok: That night you invented three different endings, and in each one the hero tricked death. In the morning you told them to the neighbors' children, who listened with their mouths open.
ev.k6_tale_later.title: The Old Tale
ev.k6_tale_later.text: One evening by the fire someone asked for a story, and suddenly you remembered the grey-haired storyteller from the square. The words came by themselves, as if they had been waiting all these years.
ev.k6_tale_later.tell: Tell it just as you heard it
ev.k6_tale_later.tell.ok: You told it in his voice, with his pauses, and at the terrifying part everyone by the fire held their breath. Afterwards they asked for more, and more.
ev.k6_tale_later.embellish: Add monsters and battles of your own
ev.k6_tale_later.embellish.success: Your monsters were more frightening than the old ones and your battles louder. The listeners barely breathed, and by morning your version was being retold in the market.
ev.k6_tale_later.embellish.failure: You got tangled in your own monsters and forgot who had beaten whom. It ended in a roar of laughter - not a bad evening either.
ev.k6_soldiers.title: An Army on the Road
ev.k6_soldiers.text: All day soldiers marched past your house: dust, tramping feet, the glint of spearheads. One of them, barely more than a boy, fell behind, sat down by the roadside and began rewrapping his blistered feet. His lips were cracked with thirst.
ev.k6_soldiers.water.ok: He drank every drop, handed back the empty cup and said, "I'll remember you." Then he caught up with the others and never looked back.
ev.k6_soldiers.spear.success: The soldier laughed and handed it over. The spear was as heavy as a log, but you stood holding it for an eternity, until his officer shouted.
ev.k6_soldiers.spear.failure: You dropped the spear right on his foot. The soldier howled and swore at you so colorfully that you learned a couple of brand-new words.
ev.k6_soldiers.hide: Hide - they say soldiers carry children off
ev.k6_soldiers.hide.ok: You sat behind the storage jars until dark, until the last footsteps faded. No one came looking for you - but it felt safer that way.
ev.k6_soldier_returns.title: The Old Soldier
ev.k6_soldier_returns.text: A weathered, sunburnt man with a scar through his eyebrow stopped at the gate. "Don't you remember me? I was the boy soldier you once brought water to. I thought of that water often - on the bad days." He untied his travel bag. "This is for you. From far away."
ev.k6_soldier_returns.welcome: Invite him to the hearth and feed him
ev.k6_soldier_returns.welcome.ok: He stayed until night, telling stories of his campaigns, and as he left he said that now he had somewhere to come back to.
ev.k6_soldier_returns.gift: Accept the gift and thank him
ev.k6_soldier_returns.gift.ok: In the bag was a finely made foreign trinket - it fetched a good price at the market. But you remember that boy's smile better.
ev.k6_far_merchant.title: A Merchant from Far Away
ev.k6_far_merchant.text: A merchant from lands so distant that not even the grown-ups knew their name had laid out his wares in the market. His face looked unfamiliar, his speech sounded like birdsong, and on his palm lay a bead - blue, clear, with a little flame inside. He caught you staring and pointed at your amulet: a trade?
ev.k6_far_merchant.trade: Trade your amulet for the bead
ev.k6_far_merchant.trade.ok: All day the bead grew warm in your fist. In the evening you looked at the fire through it, and the world turned blue and strange.
ev.k6_far_merchant.words: Learn at least a few words from him
ev.k6_far_merchant.words.success: By evening you knew five words and a little song whose meaning you didn't understand. The merchant roared with laughter and clapped you on the shoulder.
ev.k6_far_merchant.words.failure: The words wouldn't stick, and one of them, judging by the faces of the nearby traders, was rude. You kept repeating it at home until someone told you to stop.
ev.k6_far_merchant.keep: You don't trade an amulet - it was given to you at birth
ev.k6_far_merchant.keep.ok: The merchant nodded as if he understood and put the bead away. You walked off clutching your amulet, feeling somehow a little older.
ev.k6_bead_later.title: The Blue Bead
ev.k6_bead_later.text: The blue bead is still with you - on a cord, worn smooth. One day a passing trader noticed it, turned it in the light for a long time and named a price that took your breath away: glass like this, he said, is made only at the edge of the world.
ev.k6_bead_later.sell: Sell it - you couldn't earn that much in a season
ev.k6_bead_later.sell.ok: The trader paid without haggling. For a while your palm felt empty without the bead.
ev.k6_bead_later.keep: Keep it - it's a piece of your childhood
ev.k6_bead_later.keep.ok: You tied the cord tighter. Sometimes, on bad days, you still look at the fire through the bead.
ev.k6_beggar.title: The Beggar at the Gate
ev.k6_beggar.text: An old beggar sits by the gate: one leg wrapped in rags, eyes clouded white, yet his voice is surprisingly cheerful. The neighborhood children tease him and throw pebbles. In your hand is a fistful of dried fruit - your treat for the whole day.
ev.k6_beggar.share.christian: Give him half - what you give the poor, you give to God
ev.k6_beggar.share.islamic: Give him half - charity pleases God
ev.k6_beggar.share.jewish: Give him half - tzedakah is everyone's duty
ev.k6_beggar.share.dharmic: Give him half - alms are a good deed
ev.k6_beggar.share.ok: The old man felt the fruit, sniffed it and laughed: "Sweet! Who are you, generous soul?" For the rest of the day you were hungrier than usual - and happier than usual.
ev.k6_beggar.tease.success: You threw a pebble and ducked behind the others. They let you into their gang - but the old man only shook his head, and somehow that made you feel awkward.
ev.k6_beggar.tease.failure: Suddenly the old man turned his white eyes straight at you: "Aren't you ashamed?" Everyone scattered, and half the night you couldn't sleep.
ev.k6_beggar.ask: Sit beside him and ask where he comes from
ev.k6_beggar.ask.ok: It turned out he had walked half the world: he had seen mountains with ice on them in summer and people who lived on boats. By evening you hadn't even noticed that you'd shared your fruit with him.
ev.k6_acrobats.title: Traveling Players
ev.k6_acrobats.text: Traveling players have come to the market: one swallows fire, another walks a rope, a third juggles knives and cracks jokes that set the whole market laughing. Suddenly the juggler points straight at you: "You there - into the ring!"
ev.k6_acrobats.step.success: You held a little bowl on your palm while the juggler knocked nuts off it with a knife, one after another. The crowd roared, and you were rewarded with a sweet cake and a bow, as if you were a grown-up.
ev.k6_acrobats.step.failure: In your fright you tripped over the rope and sat down right in the basket of props. The whole market laughed - it was probably the best joke of the day, even if it wasn't yours.
ev.k6_acrobats.behind: Slip behind their wagons to see how they live
ev.k6_acrobats.behind.success: Behind the wagons a pot of stew was bubbling, and the rope-walker, a girl your age, was mending a costume. She taught you to stand on your hands and made you promise never to tell anyone the trick to swallowing fire.
ev.k6_acrobats.behind.failure: A huge strongman caught you by the collar, carried you back to the crowd without a word and set you down. He wasn't even angry - which somehow made it worse.
ev.k6_acrobats.watch.ok: The juggler picked someone else, who got their share of laughter and sweets. You watched from behind other people's backs and felt a little sorry.
ev.k6_flood.title: The Flood
ev.k6_flood.text: Overnight the river rose and burst its banks. By morning the water stands knee-deep on a grown man in the yards, and baskets, planks and straw float past. By the neighbors' fence a young goat is thrashing in the water - any moment now it will be swept away.
ev.k6_flood.goat.success: You waded chest-deep through the muddy water, grabbed the kid by its horn and dragged it out. The neighbor woman wept and kissed you both.
ev.k6_flood.goat.failure: The current knocked you off your feet. One of the grown-ups fished you out right at the bend; you had swallowed a lot of water and coughed for a week afterwards. The kid was pulled out further downstream - alive.
ev.k6_flood.roof: Climb onto the roof and wait for the water to fall
ev.k6_flood.roof.ok: From the roof you could see everything: flooded gardens, floating baskets, people waist-deep in water. By evening the water began to recede, leaving a dirty line on the walls.
ev.k6_flood.carry: Help carry the grain up out of reach of the water
ev.k6_flood.carry.ok: You hauled sacks and baskets up the ladder until your legs shook. Almost all the grain was saved, and for the first time the grown-ups thanked you like a real worker.
ev.k6_flood_neighbor.title: The Neighbor's Gift
ev.k6_flood_neighbor.text: The neighbor whose young goat you once rushed to save from the flood has grown very old. She called you over and led you to the best goat in her flock: "From that same line. Back then everyone stood on the bank, but you went into the water. Take her."
ev.k6_flood_neighbor.accept.ok: The goat turned out stubborn and a good milker - just like her ancestor. The old neighbor came to visit her for a long time afterwards, as if she were family.
ev.k6_flood_neighbor.refuse.ok: The neighbor grumbled, but her eyes were wet. From then on, at every feast, you were the first to get one of her cheese cakes.
ev.k6_drought.title: Drought
ev.k6_drought.text: There has been no rain since spring. The earth in the fields has cracked so wide a child's hand fits into the gaps, the well has run low, and water now has to be carried from far away. The elders say it is time for everyone to call the rain together, and the children will lead the way.
ev.k6_drought.text.christian: There has been no rain since spring. The earth in the fields has cracked so wide a child's hand fits into the gaps, and the well has run low. The priest has called for a procession around the fields with icons and banners, and the children are to walk in front and sing.
ev.k6_drought.text.islamic: There has been no rain since spring. The earth in the fields has cracked so wide a child's hand fits into the gaps, and the well has run low. The imam has called the prayer for rain in the open field outside town: everyone is to come in old clothes, children too.
ev.k6_drought.text.jewish: There has been no rain since spring. The earth in the fields has cracked so wide a child's hand fits into the gaps, and the well has run low. The sages have declared a fast and prayers for rain, and people tell of Honi the Circle-Maker, who drew a ring and would not step out of it until the rain came.
ev.k6_drought.text.dharmic: There has been no rain since the season began. The earth in the fields has cracked so wide a child's hand fits into the gaps, and the well has run low. The old women have decided, as custom demands, to marry two frogs to please the rain god, and the children will carry them from house to house, singing.
ev.k6_drought.text.buddhist: There has been no rain since the season began. The earth in the fields has cracked so wide a child's hand fits into the gaps, and the well has run low. The monks will spend three days chanting the Great Cloud sutra to call the rain, and the children are to carry water to the temple in little jugs.
ev.k6_drought.text.east_asian: There has been no rain since spring. The earth in the fields has cracked so wide a child's hand fits into the gaps, and the well has run low. It has been decided to carry the image of the dragon, lord of the waters, out of the shrine, and the children have been given willow branches to wave while they shout for rain.
ev.k6_drought.text.polytheist: There has been no rain since spring. The earth in the fields has cracked so wide a child's hand fits into the gaps, and the well has run low. The priests will make an offering to the storm god, and the children will walk around the fields with jugs, pouring water on the ground and shouting for rain.
ev.k6_drought.text.mesoamerican: There has been no rain since the season began. The earth in the maize fields has cracked so wide a child's hand fits into the gaps, and the well has run low. The priests are preparing offerings for the rain god, and the children will be led to the mountain shrine carrying flowers and copal incense.
ev.k6_drought.text.andean: There has been no rain since the season began. The earth on the terraces has cracked so wide a child's hand fits into the gaps, and the streams have run low. The priests will lead a black llama through the fields without letting it drink: let it cry out, and the sky will take pity. The children are to follow behind, singing.
ev.k6_drought.text.african: There has been no rain since the season began. The earth in the fields has cracked so wide a child's hand fits into the gaps, and the well has run low. The elders have gone to the rain-keeper with gifts, and the children are to carry water to the sacred tree and sing until they are hoarse.
ev.k6_drought.rite: Go with everyone to call the rain
ev.k6_drought.rite.success: On the third day clouds rolled in from the west and the rain poured down. The grown-ups wept and laughed, and you ran about in the downpour, head tipped back and mouth wide open.
ev.k6_drought.rite.failure: The sky stayed empty and white. You sang yourself hoarse, and afterwards you wondered for a long time why no one up there could hear you.
ev.k6_drought.water: Go with the grown-ups to the distant spring
ev.k6_drought.water.ok: Every day there and back, a jug on your shoulder. By the end of the drought you had grown taller, burned dark in the sun and learned to carry water without spilling a drop.
ev.k6_drought.sip: Secretly drink from the jug kept for tomorrow
ev.k6_drought.sip.success: No one noticed. The water was warm and tasted of clay, and you had never drunk anything so delicious in your life.
ev.k6_drought.sip.failure: Someone noticed. The grown-ups didn't scold - they only looked at you, and that was worse than any thrashing.
ev.k6_earthquake.title: The Earth Shook
ev.k6_earthquake.text: Suddenly the ground beneath you shuddered and rumbled like a huge beast. Pots tumbled from the shelves, a crack crept up the wall, and the dogs began to howl outside. You are standing in the middle of the house, and the floor is sliding out from under you.
ev.k6_earthquake.run.success: You burst out of the door just as debris came crashing down from the roof. For a long time afterwards, falling asleep, you listened for the earth to rumble.
ev.k6_earthquake.run.failure: In the doorway a falling beam struck you. A bruise across your whole shoulder and a lump on your head - but you are alive, and that's what matters.
ev.k6_earthquake.corner: Crouch in the corner by the thick wall
ev.k6_earthquake.corner.success: The wall held. When it was all over, they found you in the corner - white with dust and silent. You didn't say a word until evening.
ev.k6_earthquake.corner.failure: A shelf of pots came down on top of you. Your head was bandaged for three days, and they were sweeping up shards for a week.
ev.k6_earthquake.toy.success: You snatched it from the shelf and were the last one out. You got a scolding fit to shake the walls - the ones still standing. But the toy was safe.
ev.k6_earthquake.toy.failure: As you reached for the shelf, stones came pouring down. You were carried out in someone's arms, and for a long time you couldn't put weight on your leg.
ev.k6_street_fire.title: Fire Next Door
ev.k6_street_fire.text: In the night you were woken by shouting: the next street is on fire. The sky is orange, sparks are flying through the air, and the grown-ups have formed a chain from the well, passing from hand to hand anything that will hold water.
ev.k6_street_fire.chain: Join the chain with a small jug
ev.k6_street_fire.chain.success: You passed water until dawn, until your arms would no longer obey you. The fire was stopped at two yards, and the man leading the chain ruffled your hair in front of everyone.
ev.k6_street_fire.chain.failure: A spark landed on your arm, and the burn hurt for a whole month. But you never let go of the jug.
ev.k6_street_fire.animals: Let the terrified animals out of the neighbors' pen
ev.k6_street_fire.animals.success: You threw back the bolt, and every animal in the pen rushed past you into the darkness, bellowing. In the morning they were rounded up all over the neighborhood - alive.
ev.k6_street_fire.animals.failure: The animals milled about and wouldn't go to the door, and the smoke stung your eyes. Someone dragged you out by the arm; you coughed up soot for a long time.
ev.k6_street_fire.roof: Watch from the roof and remember
ev.k6_street_fire.roof.ok: You remembered everything: the flying sparks, the neighbors' roof caving in, its owner weeping. For years afterwards you checked the hearth twice before going to bed.
ev.k6_broken_arm.title: A Broken Arm
ev.k6_broken_arm.text: You climbed the tree for the ripest fruit at the very top, a branch cracked - and down you went. Your arm hangs as if it belonged to someone else, a lump has swollen above the wrist, and the pain makes everything go dark.
ev.k6_broken_arm.bonesetter.success: The bonesetter pulled, something clicked - you howled for the whole street to hear - then he bound your arm to splints and told you not to move it until the new moon. The bone healed straight.
ev.k6_broken_arm.bonesetter.failure: The bone healed, but slightly crooked: the arm doesn't quite straighten all the way. Still, now you know better than anyone which branches hold and which don't.
ev.k6_broken_arm.splint: Bind it to sticks yourselves and wait
ev.k6_broken_arm.splint.success: Your arm was bound to two sticks and hung in a sling. For a whole month you learned to do everything with the other hand - and the bone healed surprisingly straight.
ev.k6_broken_arm.splint.failure: The binding slipped, the bone knitted into a lump, and for a long time your arm ached at night. You got used to sleeping on your other side.
ev.k6_broken_arm.charm: Call the wise woman who charms broken bones
ev.k6_broken_arm.charm.christian: Call the old woman who heals bones with prayers and warm wax
ev.k6_broken_arm.charm.islamic: Call the old woman who sets bones and recites suras over them
ev.k6_broken_arm.charm.success: The wise woman whispered, rubbed something foul-smelling on your arm and bound it tight. A month later you were waving that same arm around as you told everyone about your fall.
ev.k6_broken_arm.charm.failure: The charm didn't help: your arm swelled up and turned blue, and the bone set crooked. The pain didn't ease until autumn.
ev.k6_arm_weather.title: The Weather Arm
ev.k6_arm_weather.text: The arm you broke as a child is aching again - it always aches the day before rain, more reliably than any soothsayer. The neighbors have started coming by to ask, "Well? Is it going to rain?"
ev.k6_arm_weather.forecast: Make forecasts - for a treat in return
ev.k6_arm_weather.forecast.success: Your arm didn't let you down once all summer. People call on you before sowing and before weddings, and the treats are enough for the whole household.
ev.k6_arm_weather.forecast.failure: Your arm lied: you promised a dry day, and the neighbors' feast was washed out by a downpour. They laughed at you until winter.
ev.k6_arm_weather.healer: Go to a healer and have it worked loose
ev.k6_arm_weather.healer.ok: The healer kneaded your arm with hot fingers, grumbling about children who climb trees. It aches less now, but before rain it still reminds you it's there.
ev.k6_sunstroke.title: Sunstroke
ev.k6_sunstroke.text: You spent the whole day running about bareheaded under a blazing sun, and by evening your head was booming like a cauldron. You feel sick, your legs are like wool, your skin is hot and dry. They have laid you in the shade, and someone is fanning you.
ev.k6_sunstroke.water: Sponge you with cool water and give you sips to drink
ev.k6_sunstroke.water.success: By night the fever broke and you fell asleep, and in the morning you woke weak but hungry - a sure sign it was over.
ev.k6_sunstroke.water.failure: The fever held for two days; you vomited and shivered and burned by turns. You recovered, but for a long time afterwards the sun made you dizzy.
ev.k6_sunstroke.healer.success: The healer gave you a sour brew to drink, covered you with wet leaves and sat beside you until morning. By dawn you were already asking for food.
ev.k6_sunstroke.healer.failure: The brew didn't help, and the fever only let go on the third day. The healer took her payment and said the sun was stronger than she was.
ev.k6_sunstroke.amulet: Hang up a charm against the noonday spirit
ev.k6_sunstroke.amulet.christian: Pray and sprinkle you with holy water
ev.k6_sunstroke.amulet.islamic: Recite suras over you and breathe on your forehead
ev.k6_sunstroke.amulet.success: By morning you felt better. The grown-ups exchanged relieved looks, and just in case, you now sit in the shade at noon.
ev.k6_sunstroke.amulet.failure: The fever wouldn't go for three days, and you lay flat as a board. You pulled through, but you remember that summer as if through a hot fog.
ev.k6_thorn.title: The Thorn
ev.k6_thorn.text: You stepped on a thorn barefoot and brushed it off at the time. Three days later your heel is swollen, red and throbbing so badly you can't put your foot down, and by evening a fever has set in.
ev.k6_thorn.healer: Call the healer to lance it
ev.k6_thorn.healer.success: The healer lanced the abscess with a knife heated in the fire, pulled out the broken thorn and showed it to you - as long as a fingernail. A week later you were running about again.
ev.k6_thorn.healer.failure: The abscess was opened, but the fever lingered for a long time, and the foot healed slowly and badly.
ev.k6_thorn.poultice: Apply steamed leaves until it draws out
ev.k6_thorn.poultice.success: On the third night the abscess burst under the bandage and the thorn came out on its own. You kept it wrapped in a rag, like a trophy.
ev.k6_thorn.poultice.failure: The leaves drew nothing. Your leg swelled up to the knee, and you were feverish for two weeks before the abscess was finally opened.
ev.k6_thorn.hide: Grit your teeth and tell no one
ev.k6_thorn.hide.success: In the night the abscess burst by itself and the thorn came out. You never told anyone - and you were very proud of yourself.
ev.k6_thorn.hide.failure: By the time you couldn't stand up, the grown-ups understood everything. They treated you for a long time - and scolded you for even longer.
ev.k6_wild_honey.title: Wild Honey
ev.k6_wild_honey.text: Bees are humming in the hollow of an old tree, and the smell of honey drifting out makes your mouth water. The older children say that if you smoke the bees out, you can grab whole handfuls of comb.
ev.k6_wild_honey.smoke: Smoke them out with a smoldering rag
ev.k6_wild_honey.smoke.success: Dazed by the smoke, the bees swirled around you, but you broke off a chunk of comb and fled. Honey ran down your chin and elbows - the best day of the summer.
ev.k6_wild_honey.smoke.failure: The bees found you before you found the honey. Your face swelled up so much that for two days you looked at the world through slits.
ev.k6_wild_honey.tell: Tell the grown-ups and let them take it
ev.k6_wild_honey.tell.ok: The grown-ups took the comb properly, with smoke and a song, and as the one who found it you got the biggest piece.
ev.k6_wild_honey.listen: Just sit and listen to them hum
ev.k6_wild_honey.listen.ok: You sat under the tree until evening. The bees flew past about their business and left you alone, as if they had accepted you as one of their own.
ev.k6_holy_place.title: At the Holy Place
ev.k6_holy_place.text: You were taken on a long journey to a holy place famous for its miracles. Several days on the road, blistered feet - and there it is: crowds of people, clouds of incense, charms and sweets for sale at the entrance. They say that here you may ask for your dearest wish.
ev.k6_holy_place.text.christian: You were taken on a long journey to a monastery that keeps the relics of a saint famous for miracles. Several days on the road, blistered feet - and there it is: crowds of pilgrims, chanting, flickering candles, little crosses and tapers for sale at the gate. They say that here you may ask for your dearest wish.
ev.k6_holy_place.text.islamic: You were taken on a long journey to the tomb of a holy man famous for miracles. Several days on the road, blistered feet - and there it is: a green dome, crowds of pilgrims, thousands of scraps of cloth tied to the grille of the tomb, each one a prayer, prayer beads and halva for sale at the entrance. They say that here you may ask for your dearest wish.
ev.k6_holy_place.text.jewish: You were taken on a long journey to the tomb of an ancient righteous man famous for miracles. Several days on the road, blistered feet - and there it is: crowds of people, candles on the stones, notes with prayers tucked into the cracks, old men singing psalms. They say that here you may ask for your dearest wish.
ev.k6_holy_place.text.dharmic: You were taken on a long journey to a famous temple beside a sacred spring. Several days on the road, blistered feet - and there it is: a gate tower taller than any tree, the ringing of bells, the scent of camphor and jasmine, garlands and sweets for offerings on sale at the entrance. They say that here you may ask for your dearest wish.
ev.k6_holy_place.text.buddhist: You were taken on a long journey to a stupa said to hold a relic of the Buddha. Several days on the road, blistered feet - and there it is: a white dome, flags fluttering in the wind, monks with prayer beads, and hundreds of people slowly circling the stupa sunwise. They say that here you may ask for your dearest wish.
ev.k6_holy_place.text.east_asian: You were taken on a long journey to a mountain shrine where a mighty spirit dwells. Several days on the road, blistered feet - and there it is: a thousand steps, gate after gate, incense smoke, wishing tablets for sale at the entrance. They say that here you may ask for your dearest wish.
ev.k6_holy_place.text.polytheist: You were taken on a long journey to the temple of a great god where, they say, an oracle gives answers. Several days on the road, blistered feet - and there it is: crowds of people, sacrificial smoke, little clay figures for offerings on sale at the entrance. They say that here you may ask for your dearest wish.
ev.k6_holy_place.text.mesoamerican: You were taken on a long journey to a sacred place where, they say, the gods were once born. Several days on the road, blistered feet - and there it is: pyramids taller than mountains, copal smoking in braziers, feathers and green beads for offerings on sale at the foot of the steps. They say that here you may ask for your dearest wish.
ev.k6_holy_place.text.andean: You were taken on a long journey to the shrine of the great oracle on the ocean shore. Several days on the road, blistered feet - and there it is: painted walls on a hill, crowds of pilgrims, shells and coca leaves for offerings on sale at the entrance. They say that here you may ask for your dearest wish.
ev.k6_holy_place.text.african: You were taken on a long journey to a sacred grove by the river where a guardian spirit lives. Several days on the road, blistered feet - and there it is: ancient trees hung with rags and shells, drums, priests in white, kola nuts and beads for offerings on sale at the entrance. They say that here you may ask for your dearest wish.
ev.k6_holy_place.offer: Leave your most precious possession as an offering
ev.k6_holy_place.offer.ok: You laid your best little treasure among hundreds of other gifts and couldn't take your eyes off it for a long time. On the way home your pocket was empty and your heart was light.
ev.k6_holy_place.wish: Ask for your own wish - in a whisper, so no one hears
ev.k6_holy_place.wish.ok: You whispered your wish three times and never gave it away, however much they asked. It stayed with you - a warm secret.
ev.k6_holy_place.wander: Slip away to watch the traders and conjurers
ev.k6_holy_place.wander.success: You saw a snake charmer, a man whose bird pulled fortunes out of a pouch, and ate something sticky and very sweet. No one noticed you were gone until you were already back.
ev.k6_holy_place.wander.failure: You got lost in the crowd and cried by the gate for half a day before they found you. You barely remember the holy place - but you'll never forget that gate.
ev.k6_shrine_wish.title: The Wish Come True
ev.k6_shrine_wish.text: Suddenly you remembered what you whispered at the holy place long ago, as a child. Strange: it came true - not the way you imagined, but it came true.
ev.k6_shrine_wish.thank: Go back there to give thanks
ev.k6_shrine_wish.thank.ok: The road seemed shorter than in childhood, and the gate lower. You left an offering and stood for a long time in the very spot where you once whispered.
ev.k6_shrine_wish.chance.ok: You smiled and shook your head. But that night, for some reason, you couldn't fall asleep for a long time.
ev.k6_owl.title: An Owl on the Roof
ev.k6_owl.text: For the third night running an owl sits on the roof and calls - long and drawn out, as if summoning someone by name. The old women shake their heads: it means trouble, a death. The grown-ups go about frowning, and the owl won't leave.
ev.k6_owl.stone: Chase it off with a stone
ev.k6_owl.stone.success: Your stone hit the edge of the roof, and the owl heaved itself up and flew off into the darkness. In the morning everyone pretended they had slept soundly, but they spoke to you more kindly than usual.
ev.k6_owl.stone.failure: The stone sailed over the roof and smashed the neighbors' pot. You were scolded longer than anyone had feared the owl - and the next night it came back.
ev.k6_owl.charm: Do everything the old women say
ev.k6_owl.charm.christian: Sprinkle the house with holy water and say a prayer
ev.k6_owl.charm.islamic: Recite the Throne Verse over the threshold
ev.k6_owl.charm.ok: You carefully repeated everything you were told, and on the fourth night the owl didn't come. The old women nodded at each other: it worked.
ev.k6_owl.look: Slip out quietly and look at it up close
ev.k6_owl.look.success: The owl turned its head almost all the way round and stared at you for a long time with yellow eyes. Somehow you weren't frightened at all.
ev.k6_owl.look.failure: The owl swooped silently straight at your face and scratched your cheek with a talon. The old women said: a mark. Ever since, you have kept well away from owls.
ev.k6_big_city.title: The Great City
ev.k6_big_city.text: For the first time you were taken to the great city. Walls taller than the tallest tree, a crush at the gates, people speaking a dozen tongues, and above the roofs rises a palace - or a temple, you never did work out which - so enormous it hurts your neck to look at it.
ev.k6_big_city.gape.success: You remembered everything: the gold on the gates, the man selling birds in cages, the smell of frying on the corner. Back home you talked about it until winter.
ev.k6_big_city.gape.failure: While you gawked, someone pinched your bundle of food. The city, it turns out, bites.
ev.k6_big_city.climb: Climb the wall to see the city from above
ev.k6_big_city.climb.success: From the wall the city looked like an anthill: roofs, smoke, people like specks. A guard brought you down - but first he let you finish looking and pointed out the palace.
ev.k6_big_city.climb.failure: A guard plucked you off the steps by the collar and promised to throw you off next time. You didn't believe him - but you didn't climb again.
ev.k6_big_city.home: Stay close to your people and beg to go home
ev.k6_big_city.home.ok: The city was too loud. You held on to the hem of a grown-up's clothes so tightly that your fingers hurt afterwards, and you only breathed freely again when you saw your own fields.
ev.k6_fawn.title: Caught in a Snare
ev.k6_fawn.text: In the thicket beyond the field a fawn is struggling - its leg caught in the noose of a hunter's snare. It cries in a thin voice, like a child, and looks at you with round, wet eyes.
ev.k6_fawn.text.ISL: In the thicket beyond the field a baby gazelle is struggling - its leg caught in the noose of a hunter's snare. It cries in a thin voice, like a child, and looks at you with round, wet eyes.
ev.k6_fawn.text.ANE: In the thicket beyond the field a baby gazelle is struggling - its leg caught in the noose of a hunter's snare. It cries in a thin voice, like a child, and looks at you with round, wet eyes.
ev.k6_fawn.text.WAF: In the thicket beyond the field a baby antelope is struggling - its leg caught in the noose of a hunter's snare. It cries in a thin voice, like a child, and looks at you with round, wet eyes.
ev.k6_fawn.text.ETH: In the thicket beyond the field a baby antelope is struggling - its leg caught in the noose of a hunter's snare. It cries in a thin voice, like a child, and looks at you with round, wet eyes.
ev.k6_fawn.free: Untangle the snare and let it go
ev.k6_fawn.free.success: Your fingers trembled, but the noose gave way. The little creature bolted into the bushes, turned back for an instant - and was gone. You told no one, and it was your first real secret.
ev.k6_fawn.free.failure: The owner of the snare caught you at it and boxed your ears: that animal was his supper. But while he was shouting, the little creature got away anyway.
ev.k6_fawn.call.ok: That evening there was meat in the pot, and everyone praised you for your sharp eyes. You ate and tried not to think about those round, wet eyes.
ev.k6_fawn.leave: Walk away - it's someone else's snare, not your business
ev.k6_fawn.leave.ok: You walked away without looking back, but that thin cry rang in your ears for a long time.
ev.k6_locusts.title: Locusts
ev.k6_locusts.text: A cloud came over the edge of the sky - but not a rain cloud. It rustled. Within an hour locusts covered the fields, the trees and the roofs, crunching underfoot and crawling into your hair. The grown-ups are beating pots and lighting fires to drive them off the crops.
ev.k6_locusts.drum: Bang a pot along with everyone else
ev.k6_locusts.drum.success: You all clattered until dark, and the swarm circled and moved on. Your field is almost untouched, and the grown-ups swear you were the loudest of all.
ev.k6_locusts.drum.failure: You banged until your palms were raw, but the locusts only left when nothing remained of the field but bare stalks.
ev.k6_locusts.roast: Gather some locusts and roast them on the coals
ev.k6_locusts.roast.ok: Crunchy, salty, a little nutty. The old man next door nodded his approval: "If they eat ours, we eat them."
ev.k6_locusts.hide: Hide indoors with your head under a blanket
ev.k6_locusts.hide.ok: It was stuffy under the blanket, and the rustling still crept in. For a long time afterwards you dreamed the walls were rustling.
ev.k6_wedding_crowd.title: A Stranger's Wedding
ev.k6_wedding_crowd.text: A rich stranger's wedding is passing down the street: musicians, lights, the bride hidden under a veil, and the groom's family throwing sweets and nuts into the crowd by the handful. Children are shrieking and diving between the grown-ups' legs.
ev.k6_wedding_crowd.grab: Push your way to the front for the sweets
ev.k6_wedding_crowd.grab.success: You stuffed the front of your shirt with nuts and sticky sweets and spent the rest of the day sharing them with the smaller children.
ev.k6_wedding_crowd.grab.failure: In the scramble someone trod on your fingers and tore your clothes, and all you got was a single empty shell.
ev.k6_wedding_crowd.lamp: Ask to carry a lamp in the procession
ev.k6_wedding_crowd.lamp.success: The master of ceremonies looked you over and pushed a lamp into your hands. You marched all the way to the groom's house, feeling part of someone else's celebration.
ev.k6_wedding_crowd.lamp.failure: The master of ceremonies just waved you away: "No outsiders." You watched the lights until they disappeared round the corner.
ev.k6_wedding_crowd.peek: Squeeze closer and peek under the bride's veil
ev.k6_wedding_crowd.peek.success: For an instant the veil swayed, and you saw a face - very young, tear-stained and smiling at the same time. For a long time afterwards you wondered how that could be.
ev.k6_wedding_crowd.peek.failure: An elderly relative of the bride smacked you on the head with a fan and chased you off with such a shriek you'd think you'd tried to steal the bride herself.
ev.k6_masks.title: The Fearsome Masks
ev.k6_masks.text: At the festival masked revelers came down the street in terrifying masks - fangs, horns, manes of straw. One of them, the most frightful of all, suddenly turned and charged straight at the children, roaring.
ev.k6_masks.text.christian: For the holiday masked mummers went from house to house: animal skins, horned masks, soot-blackened faces, jingling bells. One of them, the most frightful, with a goat's face, suddenly turned and charged straight at the children, roaring.
ev.k6_masks.text.islamic: At the festival a troupe of clowns came down the street: shaggy hats, soot-smeared faces, tambourines and wooden swords. One of them, the scariest, with fangs painted on, suddenly turned and charged straight at the children, roaring.
ev.k6_masks.text.jewish: On Purim masked revelers went from house to house: kings, queens, monsters in masks - and one, dressed as the villain Haman in a huge three-cornered hat and a painted beard, suddenly turned and charged straight at the children, roaring.
ev.k6_masks.text.dharmic: At the festival dancers in demon masks came down the street - fangs, bulging eyes, flaming manes, drums thundering. The most terrifying, the demon king, suddenly turned and charged straight at the children, roaring.
ev.k6_masks.text.east_asian: At the festival a lion dance came down the street: a huge head with bulging eyes, fringes, the thunder of drums and brass cymbals. Suddenly the lion swung round and, snapping its jaws, lunged straight at the children.
ev.k6_masks.text.mesoamerican: At the festival dancers in jaguar and eagle masks, decked in feathers and pelts, moved across the plaza to the pounding of drums. Suddenly one of the "jaguars" crouched low and sprang straight at the children with a snarl.
ev.k6_masks.run: Run off shrieking with everyone else
ev.k6_masks.run.ok: You all tore down the street in a heap, shrieking with terror and delight at once. Once you'd caught your breath, everyone wanted to do it again.
ev.k6_masks.stand: Stand your ground and stick out your tongue
ev.k6_masks.stand.success: The monster stopped, taken aback - and then bowed low to you. Everyone around burst out laughing, and for the rest of the festival you were called the monster-slayer.
ev.k6_masks.stand.failure: The monster scooped you up under its arm and carried you three houses down until you burst into tears. Then it took off its mask - it was the potter from next door. But the fright had been real.
ev.k6_masks.unmask: Sneak up behind and pull off the mask
ev.k6_masks.unmask.success: Under the mask was a sweaty lad from the next street. He laughed, let you hold the mask, and you understood: monsters can be made of wood and paint.
ev.k6_masks.unmask.failure: Someone caught your hand: the mask must not be touched, there is power in it, it brings bad luck. The elders grumbled for a long time, and you spent a whole week waiting for disaster.
ev.k6_m_sea.text: You were taken to the sea for the first time. For a long while you didn't dare go near the water that had no end, and then you scooped some up in your palm and tasted it: salty! Nobody had warned you.
ev.k6_m_caravan.text: A caravan passed down your street: pack animals under heavy bales, drivers in foreign clothes, the smell of dust, sweat and spices. You ran alongside to the very end of the road and stood watching it go for a long time.
ev.k6_m_caravan.text.ISL: A camel caravan passed down your street: bells on their necks, bales piled sky-high, drivers in foreign clothes, the smell of dust and spices. You ran alongside all the way to the gates and stood watching it go for a long time.
ev.k6_m_caravan.text.WAF: A camel caravan came in from the desert: slabs of salt strapped to their sides, drivers veiled to the eyes, the smell of dust and faraway lands. You ran alongside all the way to the market and watched for a long time as they unloaded the salt.
ev.k6_m_caravan.text.MAY: A train of porters passed down your street: tumplines across their foreheads, bundles on their backs, strange words and the smell of salt and cacao. You ran alongside to the very end of the road and stood watching them go for a long time.
ev.k6_m_caravan.text.AMR: A train of porters passed down your street: tumplines across their foreheads, bundles on their backs, strange words and the smell of dust and chili. You ran alongside to the very end of the road and stood watching them go for a long time.
ev.k6_m_caravan.text.cusco: A llama caravan passed down your street: red tassels on their ears, bundles on their backs, drivers whistling and singing. One llama spat at you, and you laughed until evening.
ev.k6_m_caravan.text.quito: A llama caravan passed down your street: red tassels on their ears, bundles on their backs, drivers whistling and singing. One llama spat at you, and you laughed until evening.
ev.k6_m_spices.text: At the market a spice-seller popped a pinch of something fiery into your mouth and roared with laughter as you hopped about. Then she gave you something sweet to chase it - and you decided the market was the best place in the world.
ev.k6_m_rainbow.text: After the rain a rainbow rose over the roofs, and you ran off to find where it ended. You didn't find it, but you came back soaked to the ears and perfectly happy.
ev.k6_m_fireflies.text: On a warm night fireflies lit up above the grass. You caught one in your cupped hands and watched the green light glow through your fingers, and then you let it go: what if it was someone's soul?
ev.k6_m_snow.text: In the morning the world had turned white. You ran out barefoot, squealed and dashed straight back in - but first you caught a snowflake on your tongue. It belonged to no one, and it melted at once.
ev.k6_m_monsoon.text: The rains came - all at once, like a wall, after long months of heat. The earth smelled so strong it made your head spin, and you danced in the downpour with all the other children until you were hoarse from shrieking.
ev.k6_m_boats.text: You sat on the bank for half a day, watching the boats going downriver. A boatman waved his oar at you, and for a week afterwards you told everyone the two of you were friends.
ev.k6_m_fortune.text: At the fair a fortune-teller grabbed your hand, traced the lines of your palm for a long time and said, "Your road is long, and your luck is short as a thread. Hold on tight." You never did work out whether that was good or bad.
ev.k6_m_monkey.text: In the square a showman was presenting a trained monkey: it bowed, beat a tambourine and went round the crowd with a little bowl. It snatched a nut right out of your hand and ate it as if that had been part of the act all along.
ev.k6_m_monkey.text.RUS: At the market a minstrel was leading a bear on a chain: it bowed, danced on its hind legs and showed how an old woman goes to fetch water. You laughed until your stomach hurt.
ev.k6_m_monkey.text.EUR: At the fair a bear-leader was leading a bear on a chain: it bowed, danced to a pipe and doffed a felt hat to the ladies. You laughed until your stomach hurt.
ev.k6_m_funeral.text: A funeral procession passed by - strangers, no one you knew. The women wailed aloud, someone sang a long slow song, and suddenly, for the first time, you understood that people die forever. That evening you held on to the grown-ups' hands for a long time.
ev.k6_m_stars.text: On a summer night you lay on the warm ground in the yard counting stars. At about three hundred you lost count, started over - and fell asleep without ever finding out how many there were.
ev.k6_m_birds.text: Birds were passing over the house - long wedges of them, calling, high, high up. The old man at the gate said they knew a road that no person knows. You wanted very much to know it too.
ev.k6_m_well.text: You shouted your name down the deep well, and the well answered - in your own voice, only duller and more frightening. You never shouted into it again, but every time you passed by, you listened.
ev.k6_m_ants.text: You spent a whole morning crouched over an ant trail: they carried seeds, a wing, a dead beetle, and not one of them was idle. You were called three times, and still you kept watching.
ev.k6_m_word.text: A foreign traveler passing through taught you a word in his language - it meant "thank you." For a week you said it to everyone: the neighbors, the dog, even the hearth.
ev.k6_m_temple.text: In the temple you looked all the way up for the first time and froze: up there in the half-light everything was painted and gilded, and it seemed that someone above was looking straight at you.
ev.k6_m_temple.text.christian: In church you looked up at the dome for the first time and froze: from the golden half-light a stern face was gazing down at you, and it seemed to see right through you.
ev.k6_m_temple.text.islamic: In the great mosque you looked up at the dome for the first time and froze: patterns ran round and round, interlacing and never ending, as if someone had written infinity in stone.
ev.k6_m_temple.text.jewish: In the synagogue the ark was opened, and you saw the Torah scrolls in their embroidered mantles, crowned with silver. Everyone stood, and you stood too, and for some reason you held your breath.
ev.k6_m_temple.text.dharmic: In the temple you came face to face with the image for the first time: huge mother-of-pearl eyes, garlands, little lamp flames. The priest struck the bell, and it seemed to you that the image blinked.
ev.k6_m_temple.text.buddhist: In the temple you looked up and froze: the Buddha sat taller than the roof of the house next door, calm, eyes half-closed, and he seemed to be smiling at you in particular.
ev.k6_m_temple.text.east_asian: At the entrance to the shrine sat two stone guardian lions with snarling jaws. You darted past them at a run, but inside it was quiet, it smelled of incense, and it wasn't frightening at all.
ev.k6_m_temple.text.polytheist: In the temple, in the half-light beyond the columns, stood the statue of the god - taller than three men, with eyes of colored stone. It seemed to you that the eyes followed you wherever you went.
ev.k6_m_temple.text.mesoamerican: For the first time your eyes followed the steps of the pyramid all the way to the top, where smoke curled up by the temple. The steps climbed into the sky, and you couldn't tell where the stone ended and the gods began.
ev.k6_m_temple.text.andean: In the temple the walls were sheathed in sheets of gold, and when the sun struck through the doorway everything blazed so brightly you had to shut your eyes. They told you: this is the house of the Sun, and it is looking at you.
ev.k6_m_temple.text.african: In the sacred grove stood a very, very old tree hung with rags and shells, and beneath it the air smelled of smoke and offerings. The old keeper said the tree remembers everyone who has ever come to it - and now it remembers you too.
ev.k6_m_lightning.text: In the night lightning struck the old tree by the road and split it in two. In the morning the whole neighborhood came running to look: the trunk was smoking, there was a smell of burning, and the old folk were breaking off splinters as charms against storms. You took one too.
ev.k6_m_crier.text: In the square a herald was crying the news: someone somewhere had won, something had gone up in price, someone had been appointed. You didn't understand a word, but for the rest of the day you shouted the very same thing, in the very same voice, from the doorstep.
ev.k6_m_litter.text: A nobleman's litter was carried down the street: embroidered curtains, servants, guards clearing the way. For an instant a curtain was drawn aside, and a ringed hand tossed a handful of nuts into the crowd. You caught one - and kept it until winter.
